minors.title: usage_out_sum is computed but never used
minors.detail: eval/score_run.py: `_finals` (lines 56, 62, 68) computes `usage_out_sum` (`sum(gen.usage.out)` per record), which ticket 10 step 8 lists as one of the four per-record sums to compute (alongside n_inject, discard.chars, discard.tokens). Unlike the other three sums, `usage_out_sum` is never read anywhere afterward - `_run_block`'s `tokens_out` field and `_paired_block`'s `tokens_out`/`base_tokens_out` all read `final.tokens_out` directly instead (also a legitimate per-record column per contract 1.1). The computed column is dead weight; not a correctness problem, but worth removing or wiring up.

minors.title: F1's fix adds a redundant full _run_block(rec) pass
minors.detail: eval/score_run.py line 179: metric_names = [k for k in _run_block(rec) if k not in ("n_records", "n_abort")] calls _run_block a second time on the whole (unfiltered) rec frame purely to read off its key names; the per-seed loop just above already computed one _run_block result per seed that has the identical key set, so before the fix no extra work was needed to get metric_names (next(iter(per_seed.values())) was free). Now, whenever rec is non-empty, _by_seed_block does one full extra sum/mean pass over all records (sums, means over every column) whose result is discarded except for its keys. This is correctness-neutral (verified: _run_block's key set is identical for n==0 and n>0) and only adds a bounded single extra O(n) pass per score_run invocation, not a repeated or O(n^2) cost, so it is a minor efficiency regression rather than a functional bug.

minors.title: refire()'s service-piece card-relocation branch can never run: the frozen-command regex only matches a loop/train shape
minors.detail: jobs/launch.py's refire() (around line 917-934) computes a `placement_kind` of 'service_agent' or 'service_probe' when the target piece's kind is 'service', anticipating that refire can relocate a dead service piece's cards. But `_parse_piece_cmd` (line 879-883) uses `_PIECE_CMD_RE`, which requires the shape `-m <module> --run-dir <dir>[ --piece i/n] 2>&1 | tee -a <log>` — the shape only `piece_command()` produces. A service piece's frozen `cmd` is built by `_agent_service_cmd`/`_probe_service_cmd`, whose shape is `-m <module> serve --run-dir <dir> --model/--agent-model ... [flags] 2>&1 | tee -a <log>` and never matches that regex (verified: `_PIECE_CMD_RE.search()` returns None on a representative agent-service command string). So any attempt to refire a service piece will always hit `_parse_piece_cmd`'s `sys.exit('could not parse the frozen command...')` before the service-aware placement logic above it is ever reached, making that branch dead code. This is a fail-loud refusal rather than silent corruption, and the ticket's own prose ('the service pieces are reused') suggests refire is meant for loop/train pieces in practice, so this is a quality/consistency issue rather than a reachable functional bug.
